study_type.claude: Mixed methods (non-randomized quasi-experiment with surveys and interviews)
study_type.nlm: Mixed methods (quasi-experimental evaluation, regression, interviews, surveys)
study_type.note: Core design is a non-randomized quasi-experiment (three onboarding cohorts), combined with rubric assessments, pulse surveys and interviews.

research_method.claude: Mixed methods: 14-month non-randomized quasi-experiment with three cohorts by onboarding date; Welch's t-test, Fisher's exact test, Holm-Bonferroni, Mann-Whitney U, covariate-adjusted OLS, sensitivity analysis; rubric competency assessments, AI-blackout tasks, monthly pulse surveys, quarterly semi-structured interviews, exit interviews
research_method.nlm: Mixed methods: quasi-experimental evaluation over 14 months with three cohorts; Welch's t-test, Fisher's exact test, covariate OLS regression, sensitivity analysis; rubric assessments, AI-blackout tasks; surveys and semi-structured interviews (32 senior engineers)
research_method.value: Mixed methods around a 14-month non-randomized quasi-experiment comparing three onboarding cohorts (Pre-AI Baseline n=35, AI-Unstructured n=22, Preceptorship n=45); AI Boost multiplier B(e) for 147 engineers with bootstrap CIs; Welch's t-test and Fisher's exact test (Holm-Bonferroni), Mann-Whitney U sensitivity, covariate-adjusted OLS; rubric competency assessments, AI-blackout tasks; monthly pulse surveys, semi-structured interviews (incl. 32 senior engineers for the competency dimensions), exit interviews

context.claude: Industry: enterprise organization of 200 engineers (mobile, web, microservices); 147 engineers for B(e); EiC cohorts 35/22/45; 12 preceptors vs. 38 non-preceptor seniors
context.nlm: Industry: enterprise organization of 200 developers (mobile, web, microservices); 147 engineers; cohorts 35/22/45; 12 preceptors, 38 non-preceptor seniors
context.value: industry; single enterprise software organization of 200 engineers (mobile, web and microservice applications) adopting agentic AI tools; 147 engineers for the AI Boost/Drag analysis, 102 early-in-career developers in three cohorts, 12 preceptors vs. 38 non-preceptor seniors

dora_applied.note: DORA only cited in related work as validated delivery predictors.

space_applied.note: SPACE only cited in related work (against unidimensional measurement).

ai_discussed.note: Agentic coding tools (Copilot, Cursor, Claude, GPT-4, MCP) and the AI Boost/Drag asymmetry are the core topic.

remote_covid.note: Work mode not reported by either.

data_window.note: Both give a 14-month observation window; only Claude gives the cohort years (2022–2023, 2024, 2024–2025), which the full text confirms, so the data span 2022–2025 rather than a single 14-month period.

cat_productivity.note: AI Boost multiplier B(e) (story points throughput composite), sprint velocity, time-to-competency.

cat_quality.note: Defect escape rate per 100 merged PRs, code review acceptance, SonarQube complexity.

cat_collaboration.note: Team knowledge redundancy score (knowledge sharing), mentoring relationships.

cat_satisfaction.note: Claude: monthly pulse surveys on engagement and psychological safety. NotebookLM lists no such measure (retention labelled Retention/DevEx; disengagement only mentioned in its framework notes). Full text confirms the pulse surveys and discussion of frustration/disengagement.

cat_activity.note: Lines of code changed per PR as the scope component of B(e); Claude also lists PR acceptance and review iteration counts.

cat_delivery.note: NotebookLM labels time to first independent feature and sprint velocity as Delivery, but these are onboarding/productivity measures; no deployment or lead-time metric.

cat_devex.note: NotebookLM says DevEx is referenced, but 'DevEx' does not occur in the full text.

cat_agile.note: Borderline: sprints and story points appear only as a throughput/velocity measure; methodology not reported.

cat_survey.note: Monthly Likert pulse surveys, semi-structured and exit interviews.

evidence.quote: A 14-month quasi-experimental evaluation across a 200-engineer organization provides preliminary evidence that structured preceptorship is associated with a 41% reduction in EiC time-to-competency relative to pre-AI baselines
A quasi-experimental design was employed comparing three cohorts within the same organization

All pairwise comparisons were tested using Welch's ttest (for continuous outcomes with unequal variances) and Fisher's exact test (for proportions), with p-values adjusted for multiple comparisons using the Holm-Bonferroni method.
These dimensions were identified through semi-structured interviews with 32 senior engineers, analysis of 450 code review interactions
The framework was implemented within a 200-engineer enterprise organization responsible for mobile, web, and microservice applications.
Empirical observation across the study population (n=147 engineers, 14-month observation period)
Phase 1 (Q1 2024) introduced GitHub Copilot; Phase 2 (Q3 2024) added Cursor with agentic capabilities and an internal multi-agent framework on Claude and GPT4
where P is a composite of throughput (story points per sprint), quality (inverse defect escape rate), and scope (lines of code changed per PR).
Defect escape rate = defects reaching production per 100 merged PRs.
Knowledge redundancy score measures the number of team members capable of maintaining each critical subsystem.
experiential data from monthly learner pulse surveys (Likert scales for engagement, perceived growth, and psychological safety) and quarterly semi-structured interviews.
